subject: Post-demo: quantized batch / cache economics — summary & next actions
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Park <alicia@monarchhealth.com>, Tom Reyes <treyes@monarchhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 02 Oct 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: quantized batch / cache economics — summary & next actions

Hi Alicia / Tom,

Thanks for taking the demo this morning — appreciate the clear product context and the emphasis on tight per-request latency for your patient-facing summarization flow. Quick recap of the items we covered and the tests we recommend to validate the cost/latency trade-offs you care about: 

TL;DR: Redwood's quantized (4-bit) runtime + small micro-batches + prefix/KV cache yields the same quality at ~35-45% lower per-1M token cost vs the hyperscaler float16 endpoint in our baseline. Latency SLOs depend heavily on batch windowing and cache hit rate.

What we saw in the demo (summary):
- Model variants: float16 (hyperscaler) vs our 4-bit quantized variant (redwood-q4).
- Baseline workload: 75% short responses (~32–64 tokens), 25% long (500–1024 tokens).
- Demo numbers (live):
  - Redwood (q4, batch=8, cache warm): ~6.8ms/token p50, ~12ms/token p95; estimated cost: $28 / 1M tokens (hosted retail estimate for this config).
  - Hyperscaler (float16, batch=1 typical): ~8.2ms/token p50, ~18ms/token p95; estimated cost: $43 / 1M tokens (on their public pricing + observed payload overheads).
- Cache behavior: warm KV cache increased effective throughput for multi-step chats — ~60% cache-hit scenarios reduced token compute by ~15–22% in our runs.

Recommended next validation tests (what Redwood will help run):
1) 1M-token synthetic run that mirrors your distribution (32/64 token short replies and 500–1024 token long replies). We will provide a harness so you can run locally and we can run in-hosted side-by-side.
2) Cold vs warm start: measure both cold-run per-token and after prefix cache warm-up across 10k sessions to estimate realistic hit rates.
3) Micro-batch sensitivity: test batch sizes [1,4,8,16] at 0ms and 50ms batching windows to see latency vs cost inflection.
4) Quality check: run the same prompts through q4 and float16 and collect top-3 qualitative diffs (we'll supply a scoring rubric).

Action items / owners:
- Redwood (Tessa): prepare bench harness + 1M-token csv + config steps (attached). Deliverable by Tue 10/05 EOD.
- Monarch (Alicia): confirm the production prompt set (or provide a sample set) and identify compliance points for data in the bench run.
- Redwood (Ben): propose a Dedicated-config econ (monthly committed) vs hosted per-token comparison once we have the 1M baseline.
- Mutual: align on an internal 2-week SLA for the bench run and a follow-up on cost delta.

Attachments: redwood-1m-token-snapshot.csv (contains token distribution + sample prompts), mutual-action-plan_Monarch_v1.docx (MVP milestones).

Looking forward to the results — happy to jump back on a quick 20m follow-up after the runs.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 03 Oct 2027 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: quantized batch / cache economics — summary & next actions

Great questions — answers below and an updated short plan.

1) Cost math detail: the $28 / 1M token figure is our hosted list estimate for the redwood-q4 runtime assuming the workload distribution I shared and a 60% effective prefix/KV cache-hit. If the hit rate drops to 30% (cold sessions / one-off prompts) we estimate ~ $38 / 1M tokens (main driver: more full-token compute on long responses). We'll include a delta table in the bench CSV for hit rates at 0%, 30%, 60%, 80%.

2) Micro-batching & short reply latency: micro-batching can increase p95 for single-shot short replies if batch windows are too long. Our recommendation for Monarch mobile flow:
  - Use batch window 0–20ms with batch size <= 8 for latency-sensitive routes. Expected p95 for 32-token replies: ~180–220ms in our q4 config (including network overhead).
  - If you cannot tolerate batching jitter, use per-request passthrough (batch=1) with slightly higher per-token cost (~+15%) but lower variance.

Updated plan / deliverables:
- Redwood (Tessa): upload bench harness + delta table + run instructions to Drive (link below). I'll also attach a short script you can run in your VPC if needed.
- Monarch (Alicia): share sanitized prompts + decision on hosted vs VPC bench by Mon 10/04 EOD.
- Redwood (Ben): draft Dedicated vs hosted pricing scenarios (commit tiers: 100k, 500k, 2M tokens/month) — deliver Wed 10/06.

If you prefer, we can run the 1M token harness in your VPC (we'll send an infra checklist) to avoid moving data. Either way the harness produces the same token-level csv so results are comparable.

Drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/Shared/monarch/quant-bench-setup

Best,
Tessa
